extracted.intended_audience: appellants, patent practitioners, and agents preparing ex parte appeal briefs to the USPTO Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing an appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 1.192(c) for an ex parte patent appeal before the USPTO Board, including required statements, arguments for each ground of rejection, appendix, and procedural/format requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of relied references (three copies)
rubrics_metrics.description: If in his or her brief, appellant relies on some reference, he or she is expected to provide the Board with three copies of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant should submit three copies of any external reference relied upon so the Board has working copies. Failure to provide required copies may be treated as a defect in the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real party in interest statement (37 CFR 1.192(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying the real party in interest, if the party named in the caption of the brief is not the real party in interest. If appellant does not name a real party in interest, the examiner will assume that the party named in the caption is the real party in interest (owner at time of filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification allows Board members to comply with ethics/conflict rules. Even if the examiner assumes the captioned party is the real party, the Board may require explicit naming. See MPEP § 1210.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related appeals and interferences statement (37 CFR 1.192(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying by application number and filing date all other appeals or interferences known to appellant, the appellant’s legal representative, or assignee which will directly affect or be directly affected by or have a bearing on the Board’s decision in the pending appeal; the appeal or interference number should also be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement is not limited to copending applications. If none are identified, the examiner will presume there are none, but the Board may require explicit identification. Provide application numbers, filing dates, and appeal/interference numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of claims statement (37 CFR 1.192(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the status of all the claims in the application, or patent under reexamination, i.e., for each claim in the case, appellant must state whether it is cancelled, allowed, rejected, etc.; each claim on appeal must be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included to avoid confusion about which claims are on appeal and their precise wording, especially where post-final amendments were sought. State status as appellant understands it so disagreements can be resolved before Board decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of amendments statement (37 CFR 1.192(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the status of any amendment filed subsequent to final rejection, i.e., whether or not the amendment has been acted upon by the examiner, and, if so, whether it was entered, denied entry, or entered in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement should reflect the appellant's understanding. It ensures clarity about post-final amendments and helps the examiner and Board resolve disagreements about claim status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of invention (37 CFR 1.192(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the invention defined in the claims involved in the appeal, required to refer to the specification by page and line number, and, if there is a drawing, to the drawing by reference characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably read the appealed claims on the specification and any drawing. Providing page/line references and drawing characters helps the Board quickly determine where the claimed subject matter is described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise statement of issues presented (37 CFR 1.192(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise statement of the issues presented for review. Each stated issue should correspond to a separate ground of rejection which appellant wishes the Board to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement must be concise but include the basis of each issue (e.g., 'Whether claims 1 and 2 are unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 103 over Smith in view of Jones' or '...unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, as being based on a nonenabling disclosure'). Do not include argument on the merits in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping of claims statement (37 CFR 1.192(c)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each ground of rejection which appellant contests and which applies to a group of two or more claims, appellant must state that the claims do not stand or fall together if he/she considers them separately patentable, and present reasons why the claims are separately patentable in the argument section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely pointing out differences is not sufficient. The appellant must (A) state the claims do not stand or fall together and (B) present arguments in the proper argument section (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8)) explaining separate patentability. Failure to do both is a concession that the ground applies equally to all claims. If appellant omits the statement but presents arguments (or vice versa), the appellant should be notified under 37 CFR 1.192(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument requirement (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant’s contentions with respect to each of the issues presented for review and the basis for those contentions, including citations of authorities, statutes, and parts of the record relied on, should be presented in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All arguments/authorities the appellant wishes the Board to consider should be included here. Arguments made first at oral hearing are normally not considered. A supplemental paper is permitted only for new authority that becomes available after filing (e.g., a new court decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument detail for 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, the brief must contain an argument which specifies the errors in the rejection and how the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112 is complied with, including how the specification and drawings, if any, support compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the errors in the §112 first paragraph rejection and indicate how the disclosure supports the claim limitations. Include citations to specification page/line and figures as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument detail for 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8)(i)/(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, the brief must contain an argument which specifies the errors in the rejection and how the claims particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which applicant regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how each claim satisfies the definiteness/claiming requirements and specify why the rejection is erroneous with reference to claim language and the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument detail for 35 U.S.C. 102 rejections (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102, the brief must contain an argument which specifies the errors in the rejection and why the rejected claims are patentable under 35 U.S.C. 102, including any specific limitations in the rejected claims which are not described in the prior art relied upon in the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the particular claim limitations not found in the cited prior art and explain why those omissions render the rejection in error. Specify the claim(s) for which no argument was provided if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument detail for 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103, the brief must contain an argument which specifies the errors in the rejection and, if appropriate, the specific limitations in the rejected claims which are not described in the prior art, and an explanation how such limitations render the claimed subject matter unobvious over the prior art. If based on a combination of references, the argument must explain why the references, taken as a whole, do not suggest the claimed subject matter and why features disclosed in one reference may not be properly combined with features disclosed in another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general argument that all limitations are not described in a single reference does not satisfy the requirements. Provide claimed-to-prior-art comparisons and reasoning why the combination would not have been made or would not produce the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument requirement for other grounds (37 CFR 1.192(c)(8)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection not falling under subparagraphs (i) to (iv), the argument should specify the specific limitations in the rejected claims, if appropriate, or other reasons, which cause the rejection to be in error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some grounds (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 101 nonstatutory subject matter) may not require citing particular claim limitations; instead explain why the rejection is erroneous with appropriate legal and factual support (example: Ex parte Hibberd).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of all arguments/authorities (37 CFR 1.192(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any arguments or authorities not included in the brief will be refused consideration by the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, unless good cause is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the brief as complete as possible. Supplemental filings are limited and typically permitted only when truly new authority emerges after filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix requirements (37 CFR 1.192(c)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing a copy of the claims involved in the appeal. The copy should be a clean copy (no brackets or underlining), double spaced, and the appendix should start on a new page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix must be at end of brief. For reissue applications, follow MPEP § 1454 for claim presentation. The brief is compliant if it includes items (1)–(9) in the order set forth (appendix last). Additional materials (list of references, table of contents, etc.) may be included but are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and heading/order requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must contain the items required by 37 CFR 1.192(c) under the appropriate headings and/or in the order indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing section headings or incorrect order are defects. If headings/items are missing or out of order, the examiner may notify the appellant (use form paragraphs such as 12.70 and subparagraphs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement (37 CFR 1.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal brief must be signed; an unsigned brief is defective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If brief is unsigned, appellant must ratify the brief within the longest of specified time periods (1 month or 30 days, whichever is longer; within time period for reply; or within 2 months from date of notice of appeal). Extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136 to avoid dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three copies of brief required (37 CFR 1.192(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Three copies of the brief are required; failure to submit three copies is a defect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If lacking, appellant must supply additional copies within the specified time periods or risk dismissal. Use form paragraph 12.13 for notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee for filing brief (37 CFR 1.17(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee for filing the appeal brief must be submitted as required; failure to timely pay the fee may result in dismissal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal may be dismissed and application abandoned if fee not timely paid and extension period exhausted. See form paragraphs 12.08–12.17 for notices relating to unpaid fees and associated consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and extensions for filing brief (37 CFR 1.192(a)/(d) and 1.136)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal brief must be filed within the prescribed period; if a brief does not comply or is not timely filed, the examiner will notify appellant and provide the longest of specified time periods to correct defects (1 month or 30 days, whichever is longer; within the time period for reply to the action from which appeal was taken; or within 2 months from the date of the notice of appeal). Extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant fails to timely file an amended brief or does not overcome notified noncompliance, the appeal will be dismissed. The appellant may petition under 37 CFR 1.181 if disagreeing with noncompliance finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed with or after appeal (37 CFR 1.116 / 1.195)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after final rejection but before jurisdiction passes to the Board may be entered if it conforms to 37 CFR 1.116; amendments introducing new matter, necessitating a new search, adding claims without canceling corresponding rejected claims, or raising new issues will not be entered. New affidavit/evidence must be in a separate paper and is governed by 37 CFR 1.195.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry of amendments after final rejection is not a matter of right. Examiners must respond to nonentered amendments and indicate the status of each claim of record or proposed. If a paper clearly places the application in condition for allowance, it should be entered and Notice of Allowability sent. Amendments received after jurisdiction has passed to the Board should not be considered by the examiner unless remanded by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review and notification of noncompliance (37 CFR 1.192(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a brief complies with the rule is within the jurisdiction of the examiner. If a brief does not comply with all requirements of paragraph (c), the examiner will notify appellant of the reasons for noncompliance and give specified time periods to correct defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may use form PTOL-462 or form paragraphs (e.g., 12.69–12.78) to notify. Appellant may file an amended brief to correct deficiencies; if appellant disagrees with the examiner’s finding, a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 may be filed. Failure to timely correct can result in dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s answer requirements and timing (37 CFR 1.193)
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner may furnish a written answer to appellant’s brief explaining the invention, references, and grounds of rejection as necessary; the examiner should furnish the appellant with a written statement in answer within 2 months after receipt of the brief. An examiner’s answer must not include a new ground of rejection (with limited exception regarding amendments entered under §1.116).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prosecution is reopened after an appeal or reply brief, appellant must either file a reply under the appropriate rule or request reinstatement of the appeal with a supplemental brief (no new amendments or evidence permitted). The examiner must acknowledge receipt/entry of a reply brief or withdraw the final rejection and reopen prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory appeal conference and recordation
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal conference is mandatory in all cases in which an acceptable brief has been filed, unless the examiner charged with preparing the examiner’s answer and the SPE conclude the appeal should not go forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should include the examiner preparing the answer, an SPE, and a conferee. The examiner’s answer should include the word 'Conferees:' followed by conferees' names and their initials next to their names. The Board will check that an appeal conference was held and may return the application to the TC Director for corrective action if the answer lacks appropriate indication.
